syllabus_topics: Introduction: challenges and opportunities of distribution
Message exchange: remote procedure calls and name management
Shared memory: memory coherence and distributed shared memory
Coordination and fault tolerance: types of faults and operational reliability, state machine replication, primary-secondary, two-phase commit
Security: introduction to cryptography, secure channels, digital certificates, TLS, distributed authentication
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 50% for the laboratory component and 50% for the theoretical component. No rounding of partial grades is performed. The laboratory component requires a minimum grade of 9.0 and consists of a project with individual grades after discussion. The theoretical component requires a minimum grade of 8.0 on the theoretical exam. For resit, the exam grade can be retaken, and it counts only if it improves the student's grade. A positive laboratory component grade (>=10) from the previous academic year can be reused.
bibliography: George Coulouris and Jean Dollimore and Tim Kindberg and Gordon Blair, Distributed Systems - Concepts and Design - 5th edition, Addison Wesley, 2011 (main)
Maarten van Steen and Andrew S. Tanenbaum, Distributed Systems - 3rd edition, CreateSpace Independent Publishing Platform, 2017 (main)
institution: Universidade De Lisboa — LERC Eng. de Telecomunicações e Informática (IST)
degree: Licenciatura em Engenharia de Telecomunicações e Informática (LERC)
